mainTopic: Whether a plain house sale includes עומקא ורומא (two proofs, both rejected), and the משנה about the בור and דות and the argument over buying a path to them.
overview: The גמרא is asking whether someone who buys a house בסתמא (without specifying) also gets the space below and above it, its עומקא ורומא. First it rejects a proof from a roof with a ten-טפחים wall: such a roof is significant on its own, so it is left out of the sale for that reason. Next רבינא brings a proof from ריש לקיש, who rules that a seller who says 'על מנת that the upper story is mine' keeps the upper story. That proof is pushed aside too: the condition only lets the seller rebuild the upper story if it falls. Then a new משנה teaches that a pit and a cistern are not sold with a house, even if the contract says 'depth and height.' רבי עקיבא says the seller must buy a path to reach them, and the חכמים say he does not. When the pits are sold to someone else, the opinions flip. The גמרא explains, through two parallel stories, that a בור is only dug while a דות is lined with built walls. Finally it starts to suggest the idea behind the path argument, and that suggestion continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: If the buyer gets the height, why does a high wall matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the idea that a plain sale includes depth and height against the rule that a roof with a ten-טפחים wall is not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think a plain sale includes depth and height, then even when the roof's wall is ten טפחים high, what difference should that make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is using the earlier rule about a walled roof to challenge the view that a buyer automatically gets the depth and height. If the buyer owns everything above, the roof should be his no matter how high its wall is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that a roof surrounded by a wall ten טפחים high is not part of the sale. If the buyer really owned the height of the house, the wall should not change anything. So that rule seems to show the buyer does not get the height.

keyTerms.meaning: it enters your mind, you might think
depth and height (the space below and above the house)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that without specification he acquires the depth and the height,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: when it is ten handbreadths high, what of it?
phrases.notes: This points back to the roof with a wall ten טפחים high, which we learned is not sold with the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ בִּסְתָמָא קָנֵי עוּמְקָא וְרוּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the walled roof as a test case for עומקא ורומא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a plain house sale includes עומקא ורומא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the buyer owns the height, the wall's height should not exclude the roof from the sale.

steps.title: A ten-טפחים wall makes the roof significant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a roof with a ten-טפחים wall counts as its own important space, so it is left out for that reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is ten טפחים high, it is significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. The roof is excluded because the wall makes it an important area of its own, not because the buyer lacks the height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A high wall turns the roof into a usable space that stands on its own, like a separate room. A separate space like that needs to be mentioned in the sale, even if the buyer normally gets the height. So the walled-roof rule tells us nothing about עומקא ורומא.

keyTerms.meaning: it is significant, it counts as important

phrases.english: Since it is ten handbreadths high,
it is significant.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the walled roof completely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The roof is excluded because it is significant, not because the buyer lacks the height.

steps.title: רבינא brings ריש לקיש's case of the upper story
steps.stepSummary: רבינא offers a new proof from ריש לקיש: a seller who says 'on condition that the upper story is mine' keeps the upper story.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear, for ריש לקיש said: This teaches that if someone sells a house and says, 'on condition that the upper story is mine,' the upper story is his.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא opens a new attempt to prove the point. He starts by quoting ריש לקיש's rule, and this sets up the proof that comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the rule sounds obvious: the seller only sold the lower floor, so of course the upper story stays his. That is why the גמרא will next ask what ריש לקיש is really adding. The proof depends on the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a source is being brought)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi,
Come and hear:
for Reish Lakish said: That is to say:
one who sells a house to his fellow,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁדְּיוֹטָא הָעֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁלִּי״ –
phrases.english: and said to him: 'On condition that the upper story is mine,'
the upper story is his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof is rejected, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a plain sale includes עומקא ורומא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's ruling about selling a house 'on condition that the upper story is mine.'

steps.title: What law is ריש לקיש teaching?
steps.stepSummary: Still inside the quoted source, the גמרא recalls asking what practical law ריש לקיש's obvious-sounding rule teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: For what law did he say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls its earlier question about ריש לקיש: if the upper story is obviously the seller's, what is the point of the rule? This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the seller only sold the house below, the upper story stays his even without a condition. So the condition must give him some extra right, and the question asks what that right is.

keyTerms.meaning: for what law? what practical difference?

phrases.english: And we said: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the ruling just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law does ריש לקיש's ruling add?

steps.title: רב זביד and רב פפא explain the extra right
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says the seller may extend beams out from the upper story. רב פפא says he may build an upper room on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: If he wants to extend projections from it, he may. רב פפא said: If he wants to build an upper room on top of it, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים each name the extra right the condition gives the seller. רבינא's proof will focus on רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב זביד, the condition lets the seller stick beams out over the courtyard, which now belongs to the buyer. According to רב פפא, it lets him build on top of the upper story. That means it is the condition that gives the seller rights in the space above.

keyTerms.meaning: projections, beams sticking out from a wall

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
that if he wants to extend projections from it,
he may extend them.
Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם רָצָה לִבְנוֹת עֲלִיָּיה עַל גַּבָּהּ –
phrases.english: that if he wants to build an upper room on top of it,
he may build.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר שֶׁאִם רָצָה לְהוֹצִיא בָּהּ זִיזִין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The condition gives the seller extra rights: extending beams (רב זביד) or building on top (רב פפא).

steps.title: Why would the seller need a condition at all?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's point: if a plain sale did not give the buyer the height, the seller would not need a condition to build above.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think a plain sale does not include the height, why do I need 'on condition'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבינא draws the proof. According to רב פפא the seller needs a condition to build above, so the buyer must normally own the height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the space above stayed with the seller anyway, building there would never need a condition. The fact that ריש לקיש requires a condition shows that a plain sale gives the buyer the height. This challenges the view that the buyer does not acquire it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ: בִּסְתָמָא לָא קָנֵי,
phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that without specification he does not acquire,
why do I need 'on condition'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ בִּסְתָמָא לָא קָנֵי לְמָה לִי עַל מְנָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב פפא's explanation to complete רבינא's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a plain sale does not include עומקא ורומא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the height stayed with the seller anyway, the 'על מנת' condition would be pointless.

steps.title: The condition lets him rebuild if it falls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the condition is still useful: if the upper story collapses, the seller may rebuild it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'on condition' helps him, because if it falls, he can rebuild it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רבינא's proof. The condition has a purpose even if the buyer does not own the height: it protects the seller's right to rebuild a collapsed upper story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the condition, the seller would only keep the upper story as it stands now. Once it fell, he would lose it. The condition keeps his right to rebuild, so ריש לקיש's ruling does not prove the buyer owns the height.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail: the walled roof is excluded because it is significant, and ריש לקיש's condition only protects the right to rebuild. The question of עומקא ורומא in a plain sale is still not proven either way.

phrases.english: The 'on condition' helps him,
so that if it falls, he can rebuild it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהֲנִי לֵיהּ עַל מְנָת דְּאִי נָפֵיל הָדַר בָּנֵי לָהּ
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The condition has a different purpose (rebuilding after a collapse), so it does not show who owns the height.

steps.title: משנה: the pit and cistern are not sold
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a house sale does not include a pit or a cistern, even if the contract says 'depth and height.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He has not sold the pit or the cistern, even if he wrote 'depth and height' for him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that the house's pit and cistern stay with the seller, even when the contract includes the depth and height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing 'depth and height' adds the space under and over the house. But a pit or a cistern is a separate item, not part of the house itself. It has to be named directly to be included in the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: a pit dug into the ground

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'depth and height' covers everything underground. It adds space, but separate items like a בור or דות still need to be mentioned by name.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַבּוֹר וְלֹא אֶת הַדּוּת –
phrases.english: Not the pit and not the cistern,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתַב לוֹ עוּמְקָא וְרוּמָא.
phrases.english: even though he wrote for him 'depth and height.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אֶת הַבּוֹר וְלֹא אֶת הַדּוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the גמרא's discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pit and a cistern are not included in a house sale, even when 'depth and height' are written.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the seller must buy a path
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules that the seller, who kept the pit, must buy a path through the buyer's property to reach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he must buy himself a path; these are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא adds that the seller has no automatic right to walk through the buyer's property to get to his pit or cistern. He has to buy that right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, the seller sold the whole house area, and keeping the pit does not automatically keep a way to reach it. So he has no right to cross the buyer's land unless he buys a path. The deeper reason behind his view is what the גמרא starts to look for in Step 17.

phrases.english: And he must buy himself a path,
phrases.notes: He means the seller, who kept the pit, needs a way through the buyer's property to reach it.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצָרִיךְ לִיקַּח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling about access to the items the seller kept.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller must buy a path to reach his pit or cistern.

steps.title: The חכמים: no need to buy a path
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree and rule that the seller does not need to buy a path.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: He does not need to buy himself a path.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי עקיבא and say the seller keeps his right to walk to his pit without paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, when the seller kept the pit, he also kept the path needed to use it. So this is a real dispute about whether a seller holds back access along with the item he keeps.
steps.whatToRemember: The pit and cistern stay with the seller. רבי עקיבא says he must buy a path to reach them; the חכמים say the path stays with him automatically.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
He does not need to buy himself a path.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא's ruling in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller keeps the path to his pit without buying it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees when the seller wrote 'except for these'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא admits that if the seller wrote 'except for these' in the sale, he does not need to buy a path to his pits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא agrees that when the seller said to the buyer 'except for these,' he does not need to buy a path.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case where even רבי עקיבא agrees the seller does not have to buy a path to reach the pits he kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, רבי עקיבא said the seller must buy a path. Here the seller openly wrote 'except for these,' even though a house sale leaves out the pits anyway. That extra wording shows he meant to keep his way of getting to them, so he does not need to buy a path.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees, admits (one side accepts a point in a specific case)
except for these (here: the בור and the דות)
to buy a path (the right to walk through the other person's land)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva agrees
when the seller said to the buyer, "except for these,"
phrases.notes: "These" are the pit and the cistern from the start of the משנה.

phrases.english: that he does not need to buy a path.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ חוּץ מֵאֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי עקיבא's ruling from Step 9 by giving a case where he agrees with the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the seller wrote 'except for these,' even רבי עקיבא agrees he does not need to buy a path.

steps.title: The reverse case: the seller sold the pits to someone else
steps.stepSummary: If the owner kept the house and sold the pits to another person, רבי עקיבא says the buyer does not need to buy a path, and the חכמים say he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sold the pits to another person, רבי עקיבא says: that person does not need to buy himself a path. And the חכמים say: he does need to buy himself a path.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case: the owner keeps the house and sells only the pits, and now the question is whether the buyer of the pits has to buy a path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the person who has to cross someone else's land is the buyer, not the seller. Here the opinions come out the opposite way from Steps 9-10. רבי עקיבא says no path needs to be bought, while the חכמים say it does.

keyTerms.meaning: he sold them (the pits) to someone else
the Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Watch out: the opinions look flipped compared with Steps 9-10. When the seller keeps the pits, רבי עקיבא says a path must be bought. When the pits are sold to someone else, רבי עקיבא says no path is needed, and the חכמים say one is needed.

phrases.english: If he sold them to another person,
phrases.notes: Here the owner keeps the house and sells only the pit and the cistern.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
he does not need to buy himself a path,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: he does need to buy himself a path.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְכָרָן לְאַחֵר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror case of Steps 9-10, with the two opinions reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the pits are sold to someone else: רבי עקיבא says no path needs to be bought, and the חכמים say a path must be bought.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the opinions flip, the גמרא will soon try to find the one idea that explains both cases.

steps.title: רבינא asks why both a pit and a cistern are listed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא is bothered that a בור and a דות seem to be the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: רבינא sat and had a difficulty: a בור is the same as a דות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבינא asks why the משנה (Step 8) names both a בור and a דות if they are the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה usually does not list two words for one thing. If בור and דות mean the same object, listing both seems like extra words. This question pushes us to define each word.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion that explains the משנה
it was difficult for him (he had a question)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Ravina sat, and he had a difficulty:
A pit is the same as a cistern!

steps.triggerLanguage: יְתֵיב רָבִינָא וְקָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ הַיְינוּ בּוֹר הַיְינוּ דּוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by questioning the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of both בור and דות (Step 8).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two words mean the same thing, one of them is extra.

steps.title: רבא תוספאה explains the difference from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא תוספאה quotes a ברייתא: both are in the ground, but a בור is just dug and a דות is built.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא תוספאה said to רבינא: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: both a בור and a דות are in the ground, except that a בור is made by digging and a דות is made by building.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא תוספאה answers רבינא with a ברייתא that shows the two words mean different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are holes in the ground, so they look alike. The difference is how they are finished. A בור is only dug out, while a דות has built walls lining the inside. So the משנה names two different things.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a source that answers the question)

phrases.english: Rava Tosfa'a said to Ravina:
Come and hear, as it is taught:
Both a pit and a cistern are in the ground,
except that a pit is made by digging
and a cistern is made by building.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא תּוֹסְפָאָה לְרָבִינָא תָּא שְׁמַע דְּתַנְיָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the terms from a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בור and דות are the same thing, so one word is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בור is only dug out, and a דות is lined with built walls, so the משנה names two different things.

steps.title: רב אשי asks the same question
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי, at a different time, is bothered by the same question: a בור seems to be the same as a דות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי sat and had a difficulty: a בור is the same as a דות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story with the same question, this time asked by רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is being asked here. The גמרא is recording that the same question came up again with a different scholar, and it is setting up the answer that comes next.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב אָשֵׁי וְקָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi sat, and he had a difficulty:
A pit is the same as a cistern!

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב אָשֵׁי וְקָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ הַיְינוּ בּוֹר הַיְינוּ דּוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question of Step 13 in a second, separate story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of both בור and דות (Step 8).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two words mean the same thing, one of them is extra.

steps.title: מר קשישא gives the same answer
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא בריה דרב חסדא answers רב אשי with the same ברייתא: a בור is dug and a דות is built.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא, son of רב חסדא, said to רב אשי: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: both a בור and a דות are in the ground, except that a בור is made by digging and a דות is made by building.
steps.whatsHappening: מר קשישא answers רב אשי with the exact same ברייתא that רבא תוספאה used in Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is word for word the same as in Step 14. The גמרא is simply reporting a second story where the same question got the same answer. Nothing new is added to the law.

keyTerms.meaning: מר קשישא, the name of an אמורא

steps.whatToRemember: A בור and a דות are both holes in the ground. A בור is just dug out, and a דות is lined with built walls. That is why the משנה lists both.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Chisda, said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear, as it is taught:
Both a pit and a cistern are in the ground,
except that a pit is made by digging
and a cistern is made by building.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי תָּא שְׁמַע דְּתַנְיָא

steps.title: What are רבי עקיבא and the חכמים really arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the מחלוקת about buying a path again, and starts to suggest what it is based on.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And he must buy himself a path; these are the words of רבי עקיבא. And the חכמים say: he does not need to, and so on.' What, is it not about this that they disagree...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the מחלוקת from Steps 9-10 and starts to suggest the idea behind it. This line is a setup, and the suggestion itself comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not repeat the משנה just to review it. It quotes it again to ask what the real reason for the argument is. The words 'מאי לאו' show that the גמרא is about to offer a suggested explanation, which may later be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: the words of (marks whose opinion this is)
and so on (the quote continues as in the משנה)
what, is it not that... (introduces a suggested explanation)
